seal.statement: In the failing formation traced in the second causal packet of 2026-09-19, the seed's admin control snapshot stays stale_usable for 167 s because some active or ready node's ready lease has lapsed, a fact about the cluster that the cache repair it triggers can never clear, and the seed's lease sweeper declines on every sweep to reconcile that node while its transport is connected. Neither says which node, how far past expiry its lease is or for how long this has held, the admin control snapshot has no logger at all, and the admission observer carries the ready-lease witness only on its final snapshot. This quest makes those observable without changing them. The control snapshot's stale watermark logs each transition - set, naming the node, its status, its connection state and how far past expiry its ready lease is; a change of the named node; cleared, with how long it was set - and never each evaluation. The existing line for a skipped lease disconnect of a transport-connected node states how far past expiry the lease is and for how long that node has been skipped consecutively. The admission observer records the ready-lease witness on every transition of its observation state. No decision, schedule, retry cadence, repair trigger, log message text or existing log field changes.

text: Observability only. New src/admin/admin-control-snapshot-stale-watermark-record.js states the stale watermark's set / node_changed / cleared transitions once each, with the node, status, connection state, lease age, how long it was set and the suppressed-evaluation count, from per-owner WeakMap state and the deciding evaluation's own observation time; the control snapshot owner receives a logger the way AdminServiceDiscovery does. The lease sweeper's existing skip line gains leaseExpiredForMs and skippedForMs from a per-node map pruned to the nodes the last sweep skipped. The admission observer's transition records carry a bounded projection of the ready-lease witness, outside the fingerprint. Witnesses: four node:test files plus a differential against main (test/diagnostics/lease-liveness-decision-grid.js + .golden.json generated on f9d388499 before any src change).

round 1 REJECT (4 blocking; no changed decision - three differentials against the sealed base: 6359 watermark evaluations over five paths with every cache read counted, 300 sweeper sequences, 13726 observer transitions, all 0 differences; the golden regenerates byte-identical on main). B1 decision-neutral: the watermark recorder calls logger.info and reads owner.logger.info unguarded where main had no logger; a throwing logger makes evaluateAuthoritativeControlSnapshotRepair and resolveControlSnapshot throw (real AdminWebSocketAPI with a synchronously throwing log flush: 3 of 3 resolveLocalControlSnapshot requests rejected where main resolves), and the record commits after the emit so the throw repeats on every evaluation. B2 statement 'for how long that node has been skipped consecutively': pruneLeaseSkipObservations runs only after the loop completes, and the real owner re-throws gateway failures, so a renewal or a deleted row during a rejecting sweep is never forgotten - a line reads leaseExpiredForMs 1000 with skippedForMs 45000, a deleted node stays in the map; 24 lenient / 287 strict violations in 2311 skip lines. B3 statement 'cleared, with how long it was set': the recorder is keyed per owner and assumes observation times increase, but snapshots stamp capturedAt before awaiting diagnostics and requests are not single-flight; two concurrent real requests with one slow readiness read give set, cleared with setForMs -5000, set, cleared with 51000 for one lapse and one renewal; 10 negative durations in 300 random sequences. B4 R19: deleting the one production line 'logger: this.logger' in admin-websocket-api-base.js leaves all five receipts green - production would emit nothing and no witness would notice (the wiring is present today; its proof is absent). Non-blocking: the real LoggingService forces top-level nodeId to the emitting node, so the stale node lands under contextNodeId - use a role-specific key such as staleNodeId; a merged observer run keeps the first witness, so a node change inside the run is invisible; receipt 5 alone does not kill 'witness in the fingerprint' nor 'skip state enters the decision after 60 s' (grid horizon 15 s against a traced 166 s); surviving mutants: suppressed count never reset across a transition, the no-leader clear removed; receipt digests omit the grid module and its golden; stop() does not clear the skip map; the repairTables golden column witnesses nothing. Packet-relevant, confirmed on main: the watermark also fires for connection_state connected and for absent lease evidence; a row the sweeper already disconnected (status active, disconnected, lease null) keeps the watermark set indefinitely; status 'ACTIVE' with a live lease sets it too because the predicate lowercases the status while isNodeRecordReady compares the raw value.

Round-1 rejection repaired, observability only. B1: the recorder now reads the logger inside a guard (a throwing getter or proxy is a real shape), commits the record BEFORE it emits, and counts a failed emission instead of raising it - both call paths return exactly what main returns for seven logger shapes, and a sink that re-enters the owner cannot replay the transition being emitted. B2: the skip run is broken by a renewal (including to a time already past), a disconnect, a departed row or any sweep that did not skip the node, reconciled in a finally so a rejecting sweep counts, with stop() and a non-leader sweep clearing the map; 0 <= skippedForMs <= leaseExpiredForMs now holds on every line. B3: an observation older than the last committed one is counted, not acted on, so one lapse and one renewal are one set and one cleared with a non-negative setForMs under concurrent requests. B4: receipt 1 drives the REAL AdminWebSocketAPI through the REAL LoggingService into a log file, so deleting the logger dep turns it red. N1 staleNodeId/previousStaleNodeId and skippedNodeId survive buildConsolePayload; N2 merged runs carry the latest witness and a change count; N3/N4 the golden was regenerated on a git archive of f9d388499 with a 170 s sweeper horizon and a merging poll pair, and receipt 5 alone now kills both surviving mutants; N5/N6/N9 second cycle, no-leader clear, grid+golden digests, and a narrowed repair-table column. A lease that has not lapsed is a named state, never a negative age.

Out of scope (R17), for the owner: the complexity ratchet now measures 1817 against its 1818 baseline and prints the tighten hint, because extracting disconnectExpiredLeaseHolders took sweepExpiredLeases from 13 (its value on main) to under the threshold. The one-line tightening is in scripts/check-complexity.js, which this epic's authorizes list does not cover, so it is left for the owner rather than absorbed.

Production findings recorded, not fixed (the predicate is a decision): resolveControlSnapshotCacheStaleWatermark fires for a row the lease sweeper has already disconnected (status active, connection_state disconnected, ready_lease_expires_at null) and holds indefinitely, and it fires for status 'ACTIVE' with a LIVE lease because the predicate lowercases the status while isNodeRecordReady compares the raw value. The lines stay truthful in both: the first says readyLeaseState unavailable with reason ready_lease_expiry_unavailable, the second says leaseAgeState not_expired with readyLeaseAgeMs -30000 and leaseExpiredForMs null.

round 2 REJECT (1 blocking, mechanical). All four round-1 blockers re-proved repaired with the verifier's own scripts and every decision still identical to main: B1 six further hostile logger shapes incl. throw null, a rejecting async info, a re-entrant sink, a sink that deletes owner.logger and a stack overflow - decisions identical, nothing thrown, commit-before-emit killed by receipt 1, either guard removed killed by receipt 5; B2 the repaired definition of 'skipped consecutively' accepted (a run of consecutive sweeps that skipped the node; leaseExpiredForMs carries the other reading) - rebuilt oracle over 450 sequences, 18192 skip lines, 0 violations, invariant 0 <= skippedForMs <= leaseExpiredForMs 0 violations, and the extracted disconnect loop is decision-neutral under 1204 forced mid-loop rejections with a global call sequence compared (0 differences; sweepExpiredLeases complexity 13 -> 4); B3 independent recorder model over 14049 evaluations incl. 2187 out-of-order and 1303 tied: 0 mismatches, 0 negative durations, a genuinely newer state is delayed to the next in-order poll, never lost; B4 deleting the logger injection turns receipt 1 red, 10 of 10 runs pass, no handle left. NEW B5 (R13): the receipt-1 test creates a temp directory with a log file on every run and never removes it (16 -> 26 directories after ten runs). Non-blocking: three unpinned behaviours whose mutants survive all four witness files (a tie dropped as out of order, a not-expired lease printed as a negative leaseExpiredForMs by the recorder, the backwards-clock clamp on skippedForMs removed); a rejecting ASYNC info leaves an unhandled rejection (the real LoggingService.info is synchronous); a one-hour backwards clock step mutes the recorder until the clock passes its high-water mark (decisions unaffected); the skip line's role key is asserted on a fake logger, only the watermark line through the real sink; readyLeaseWitnessChangeCount increments on every poll while a lease is lapsed because it compares the age; a comment says the map reconciles however the sweep ends but a sweep whose read throws exits before the try; the repairTables grid column still witnesses nothing. Golden regenerates byte-identical from a fresh extract of the sealed base; the two digest-binding receipts cannot mask a sealed one; 35 mutations, 32 killed; statics green; 30 suites green; evidence size bounded (two fixed-size projections per entry, cap unchanged).

Backwards-clock mute, recorded as a finding and deliberately not fixed here: after a large backwards step of the control snapshot owner's supplied clock, the watermark recorder classes every evaluation as out of order until the clock passes its high-water mark again, so a transition inside that window is not reported at the moment it happens. No decision is affected - the recorder hands every watermark straight back - and the count is not lost: the next line that does get out states outOfOrderObservations. Adding logic for it would mean choosing between a negative duration and a re-anchoring rule, which is a behaviour question for the owner rather than an observability repair.

Round-2 rejection repaired. B5: the receipt-1 harness now owns the temp directory it creates and removes it in the existing finally, after shutdown, through a guarded removeLogDirectory() that records a failure instead of throwing over the assertion that failed; the test then asserts the directory is gone. The 62 stale lagrange-watermark-* directories were deleted and ten consecutive runs leave the count at 0. The other three new test files create no temp directories. NB1: three unpinned behaviours now have pins that kill their mutants - a tied observation time still reports its transition, a lease that has not lapsed prints leaseAgeState not_expired with a null leaseExpiredForMs and a signed readyLeaseAgeMs, and a backwards clock step clamps skippedForMs to 0 without restarting the run. NB2: the skip line's role key is asserted through the real LoggingService sink, where nodeId is the emitter, contextNodeId is the pre-existing passed value and skippedNodeId names the skipped node. NB3: readyLeaseWitnessChangeCount now compares the named node and the lease state, not the age. NB4: a thenable returned by info gets a no-op rejection handler that counts the failure - 6 emissions through a rejecting async sink now produce 0 unhandled rejections, as on main. NB5: the lease-service comment says a sweep whose read throws never reaches the finally. NB6: the inert repairTables column is dropped with the reason in a comment and the golden regenerated on main's sources. NB7 is recorded as a finding, not fixed.

round 3 APPROVE (0 blocking) on index tree 942a203e3aa0da23df4ad22cfe9eb109522040c8 at f9d388499. Each of the four round-1 failures stays repaired: (1) a logger failure cannot affect the decision - every round-1 shape, six round-2 shapes, eleven thenable shapes and the real LoggingService with a synchronously failing flush give main's decision on both call paths with nothing thrown, identical microtask ordering and no added await; removing either guard or emitting before the commit is killed by the quest's receipts; (2) durations are truthful after partial sweeps - 450 sequences, 1204 forced mid-loop rejections, 18192 skip lines, 0 oracle violations, 0 violations of 0 <= skippedForMs <= leaseExpiredForMs; (3) overlapping snapshots cannot invent transitions - two concurrent real requests finishing out of order give exactly one set and one cleared with setForMs 55000; 14049 evaluations incl. 2187 out of order and 1303 tied, 0 model mismatches, 0 negative durations; (4) the production API and logging wiring is exercised and not bypassable - receipt 1 constructs the real AdminWebSocketAPI and LoggingService writing a file, and deleting the injection or dropping the injected logger turns it red; the skip line is asserted through the real file sink. The quest acquires no authority over readiness or repair decisions: the only edits to pre-existing decision files are two return wrappers handing back the same frozen watermark, a logger field with its one-line injection, and the verbatim extraction of the disconnect loop; the added state and fields are read only inside the four files that own them; three differentials against the sealed base show 0 differences (watermark 6359 evaluations over five paths with every cache read counted, sweeper with a global call sequence, observer 13726 transitions with 7735 merged runs of differing witnesses); the report JSON is byte-identical to main's once the added keys are removed and formationVerdict is identical; mutants that make a diagnostic decide are killed by receipt 5. B5 repaired: both temp prefixes count 0 before and after ten runs, also with a forced failing assertion, the original failure being the one reported. 40 verifier mutants, 0 survive; golden regenerated byte-identical from a fresh sealed-base extract (sha256 11a7e2b1...); statics green; 30 suites green.
